title: Spanish Black Pine: Ancient Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: A mountain pine of inland Spain. The Pino del Aprisquillo, 350 to 450 years old by its accounts, was voted Spain's Tree of the Year in 2016.
intro: The Spanish black pine is a mountain pine of inland Spain, and the old ones here all take a walk to reach. The Pino del Aprisquillo above La Adrada, in the foothills of the Sierra de Gredos, was voted Spain's Tree of the Year in 2016; accounts put it at 350 to 450 years, and nobody has counted the rings. Three stand in the Sierra de Cazorla. Families from scattered farmhouses once heard Sunday Mass under the low-forked Pino de la Misa. Muleteers cut marks into the bark of the Pino de las Cruces to tell those behind them they had passed. A stone beside the third, at 1,640 metres, carries the name of the naturalist Felix Rodriguez de la Fuente, who filmed nearby in the 1970s. Near Girona, a 29-metre pine in the wet Guilleries was protected in 1990 on the same day as an oak 480 metres away.
